**Live specimen, recorded for triage — not a claim and not a grade.** From the `domain:devx` PM seat (`session_01F8q5J1MQyocgtNspb15fSn`).

Draft PR #6921 (issue #6673) changes **two diagnostic message strings** in `packages/lint/src/validate-searchable-fields.ts` plus their pinned tests — 43 additions, 3 deletions, one package. The Docs Drift Check on it posted:

> This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`.
> **3** hand-written doc(s) reference the affected code and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:
> - `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx` _(via @objectstack/lint)_
> - `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` _(via @objectstack/lint)_
> - `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` _(via @objectstack/lint)_

None of the three concerns `searchableFields`, the two rules whose hints changed, or anything the diff touches. The edge that produced all three is `via @objectstack/lint` — the package, not the symbol — which is exactly the granularity this card is about, reproduced on a diff about as small as one can get.

⚠️ **One detail worth carrying into whatever fix lands: the third row points at a file that a code PR is forbidden to edit.** `content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` is covered by the repo's "never edit `content/docs/releases/` in a code PR" directive (CLAUDE.md; the merge-conflict-magnet rule). So on this class of PR the advisory does not merely over-list — it names a target where acting on it is the wrong move, and a dev who treats the list as a worklist is being steered toward a prohibited edit. Whether the fix is symbol-level edges, a `releases/**` exclusion, or both, the releases path seems worth excluding on its own merits regardless of how the granularity question resolves.

The advisory is correctly marked "Advisory only" and blocks nothing; PR #6921 is taking no action on it, which is the right call.

⛔ Not graded here — this card carries `finding` and grading is triage's call. Recorded only because the specimen is fresh and would otherwise be lost when the PR merges.

Triage (maintainer-authorized one-off pass, 2026-08-09, registered on #6015): **promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`** (`domain:devx` kept). Measured twice in one hour: a 112-doc advisory on every spec-touching PR is a signal readers have already learned to skip, which silently disables the check exactly where drift risk is highest. Deliverable: finer granularity for the hub packages (file-level or export-level mapping, or a capped summary with a drill-down artifact) so the advisory stays readable where it is currently noise.

**Second specimen preserved here before #7003 merges** (handed to this dev seat by the `domain:devx` PM seat; recording it so it survives the PR). Measured against the fix in flight on `claude/issue-6893-docs-drift-granularity`.

PR #7003 (issue #6795) is a **one-line JSDoc wording change** in `packages/client/src/index.ts` — no behaviour, no export, no type. Docs Drift Check reported **14** docs, **3 of them release-owned** (vs 1 of 3 on the #6921 specimen).

Measured before/after with the branch's mapper:

```
BEFORE:  14 docs, one flat list (3 of them targets a code PR must never edit)
AFTER:   14 total | 11 editable + 3 read-only  (partitioned, nothing dropped)
```

Three things this specimen settles:

1. **The forbidden-path hazard is not a corner case.** 3 of 14 rows here. The fix in flight moves them under an explicit ⛔ read-only heading that says "file an issue, do not edit here", rather than filtering them out — see below.
2. **The residual granularity complaint is real and survives this PR.** A one-sentence JSDoc edit still flags 11 editable docs, because nothing in the fix narrows the package→doc edges. That half is being filed as its own card with this specimen attached.
3. **Both edge kinds behave identically, by construction.** Twelve rows come from the npm name (`via @objectstack/client`), two from the repo path (`via packages/client`). The read-only partition is computed from the **doc's own path**, never from the edge that produced it, so there is no half-fix risk here — verified: all 3 release rows in this specimen are name-edges and all 3 partition correctly, while both path-edge rows stay in the editable list where they belong.

⚠️ One correction to the direction sketched on this card, with evidence. **Excluding `content/docs/releases/**` from the output is the option #4920 already considered and rejected**, one level up in the same toolchain — `scripts/docs-audit/check-audit-scope.mjs` fails the build if those pages leave the audit scope, and says why:

> Release pages are meant to be IN scope and READ-ONLY (#4920): audited, never edited, findings filed as issues. An empty set means either the pages moved, or they were excluded from the scope — the option that ruling rejected, because it leaves the most-read pages in the docs unaudited with nothing to say so.

So the fix in flight applies #4920's shape rather than contradicting it: the pages stay in the computed set (`docs` in `--json` is unchanged, and it is what scopes the audit), and what forks is the **deliverable** — a separate read-only section in the PR comment. `releaseOwnedDocs` is a partition of `docs`, never a filter.
